Escalate to the AD/GPO owner.\\\\n- **Antivirus / EDR interference** (`0x80070005` access denied, `0x80070020` file in use, CBS\\\\n  \\\\\"access denied\\\\\" on WinSxS): AV real-time scanning locks files TrustedInstaller must replace, or\\\\n  the **Spectre/Meltdown `QualityCompat` registry key is missing** (Microsoft won\\'t offer updates\\\\n  without it). GPO disabling/redirecting WU \\\\u2192 read [gpo blocks](reference/gpo-blocks.md).\\\\n  - AV/EDR file locks / QualityCompat \\\\u2192 read [av interference](reference/av-interference.md).\\\\n  - BitLocker / boot-critical update \\\\u2192 read [bitlocker](reference/bitlocker.md).\\\\n  - 2012 R2 SHA-2 / exec-policy / ACL / DCOM / other \\\\u2192 read [sha2 and misc blockers](reference/sha2-and-misc-blockers.md).\\\\n\\\\n## Ordered recovery\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: **Establish the 2012 R2 SHA-2 baseline first** if applicable \\\\u2014 nothing else patches on 2012 R2 until KB4490628 + KB4474419 are in.\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: **Suspend BitLocker for one reboot BEFORE** any boot-critical/firmware update (confirm the recovery key is available first).\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: **Clear the AV/policy block** \\\\u2014 add the QualityCompat key / WU exclusions (or vendor-console exclusions), and clear the GPO registry values for this cycle.\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: **Verify** the block is cleared (write test to WU dirs, policy values cleared, BitLocker suspended) and note anything that will revert.\\\\n\\\\n## Validation (check your own work before reporting success)\\\\n- [ ] The specific control was identified (GPO vs AV vs BitLocker vs SHA-2), not treated generically.\\\\n- [ ] For BitLocker: protection is **Suspended for the reboot** and the recovery key is confirmed available (never reboot a protected boot-critical patch blind).\\\\n- [ ] For AV: the QualityCompat key is present (2012 R2/2016) and a write test to `SoftwareDistribution`/`WinSxS` succeeds.\\\\n- [ ] For GPO: values are cleared for this cycle AND you have flagged that the GPO must be fixed (or it reverts in ~90 min).\\\\n- [ ] The originally failing scan/install no longer fails on the control.\\\\nIf any check fails, re-classify; do not leave AV disabled or BitLocker suspended beyond the patch window.\\\\n\\\\n## Gotchas\\\\n- **Clearing a GPO registry value is temporary** \\\\u2014 a domain GPO restores it on the next refresh (~90 min / reboot). The durable fix is the GPO (or moving the instance to a patching OU) \\\\u2014 escalate to the AD team.\\\\n- **BitLocker must be suspended BEFORE a boot-critical/firmware update, not after** \\\\u2014 otherwise the reboot changes PCR measurements and demands the 48-digit recovery key (via serial console). {$_.DisplayName -match \\'CrowdStrike|Symantec|McAfee|Carbon|SentinelOne|Trend|Sophos|Cylance|Defender|ESET|Kaspersky\\' -and $_.Status -eq \\'Running\\'} | Select DisplayName,Name\\n# Defender exclusions for WU paths (on-box):\\nif((Get-Service WinDefend -EA SilentlyContinue).Status -eq \\'Running\\'){\\n  \\'SoftwareDistribution\\',\\'WinSxS\\',\\'System32\\\\catroot2\\' | % { Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath \"$env:SystemRoot\\\\$_\" -EA SilentlyContinue }\\n  # temporary, patch-window only:\\n  Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -EA SilentlyContinue\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## Verify write access\\n```powershell\\n$t=\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\SoftwareDistribution\\\\wtest_$(Get-Random).tmp\"\\ntry{ [IO.File]::WriteAllText($t,\\'x\\'); Remove-Item $t -Force; \"WRITE OK\" }catch{ \"AV STILL BLOCKING: $($_.Exception.Message)\" }\\n```\\n\\n## Escalation / cleanup\\n- **Third-party AV/EDR exclusions are set in the vendor console, not locally:** CrowdStrike (Falcon Console), Carbon Black (approved list for svchost/TiWorker), Symantec/Broadcom (exclude TrustedInstaller.exe/TiWorker.exe).\\n- Dual-AV (Defender + third-party) \u2192 disable Defender via GPO.\\n- **Re-enable real-time protection after the window:** `Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false`.\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "e29e5668-4808-4107-97ed-1c172b540da8", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's what's going on, and the fix in order.

## Why Microsoft shows 0 applicable updates

On Windows Server 2016 (and 2012 R2), Microsoft gates update delivery behind an **AV-compatibility registry key** tied to the Spectre/Meltdown mitigations — the `QualityCompat` key. If that key isn't present (or isn't set to `0`), Windows Update's scan engine won't even offer updates as "applicable" — it's not a connectivity or WSUS/SSM problem, it's Microsoft deliberately withholding updates until it believes your AV is compatible. Third-party AV products are supposed to set this key themselves after certifying compatibility; many never do, or do so inconsistently, which is almost certainly why your scan returns zero every time.

## Why installs fail with 0x80070005

That's a separate but related symptom: your AV's real-time scanning engine is locking files inside `WinSxS` (or `SoftwareDistribution`/`catroot2`) while `TrustedInstaller`/`TiWorker` tries to replace them during install, so the file-system call gets access-denied.

## Fix, in order

**1. Set the QualityCompat key first** — this unblocks the scan itself:
```powershell
$qc='HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\QualityCompat'
$v=(Get-ItemProperty $qc -Name 'cadca5fe-87d3-4b96-b7fb-a231484277cc' -EA SilentlyContinue).'cadca5fe-87d3-4b96-b7fb-a231484277cc'
if($v -ne 0){ New-Item $qc -Force|Out-Null; Set-ItemProperty $qc -Name 'cadca5fe-87d3-4b96-b7fb-a231484277cc' -Value 0 -Type DWord; "QualityCompat key set" } else { "QualityCompat OK" }
```
Re-run a scan after this — you should start seeing applicable updates.

**2. Clear the AV file-lock for installs** — since it's third-party, exclusions need to be added in **the vendor's management console**, not locally on the box:
- CrowdStrike → Falcon console
- Carbon Black → approved list for `svchost.exe` / `TiWorker.exe`
- Symantec/Broadcom → exclude `TrustedInstaller.exe` / `TiWorker.exe`

Exclude these paths: `%SystemRoot%\SoftwareDistribution`, `%SystemRoot%\WinSxS`, `%SystemRoot%\System32\catroot2`.

**3. Verify the lock is actually cleared** before retrying the install:
```powershell
$t="$env:SystemRoot\SoftwareDistribution\wtest_$(Get-Random).tmp"
try{ [IO.File]::WriteAllText($t,'x'); Remove-Item $t -Force; "WRITE OK" }catch{ "AV STILL BLOCKING: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
```

**4. Re-run the patch.** If it still fails 0x80070005, the AV's kernel-mode driver (not just the console exclusion) may need a temporary pause for the install window — that has to be done through the vendor's tooling since it's third-party, not Defender.

One flag: if you also have Defender running alongside the third-party AV (dual-AV), that combination itself can cause lock contention — Defender should be disabled via GPO in that case.

Want me to check this specific instance's AV service and QualityCompat key state over SSM, or pull the actual patch failure logs to confirm it's this exact signature?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
